sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1.2 'Rappel phonologique' (pp.41-42) gives consonant/vowel charts, the palatalisation prosody and 'Il y a deux tons phonologiques. Seul le ton haut est marque.'; sec. 1.3 describes tone perturbation of words after pause and final-vowel -> -a before pause; sec. 4.6 'Ton' (pp.97-98) verb tone classes. No mention of accent/stress anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent + read).

sources.citation: Swackhamer, Jeanette. 1991. Tonal behavior of Podoko verbs in independent clauses. In Stephen C. Anderson (ed.), Tone in five languages of Cameroon (SIL/UTA Publications in Linguistics 102), 93-125. Dallas: SIL & University of Texas at Arlington. SIL archives 8917.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. 'Like many Chadic languages, Podoko has basically a two-tone system' with downstep of L (three heights, two registers), phrase-final downtilt, clause-initial grammatical downstep marking present tense (spectrograph evidence), clause-final 'intonation' variants noted in passing; 627-verb tone-class appendix.

sources.citation: Wolff, Ekkehard. 1987. Consonant-tone interference in Chadic and its implications for a theory of tonogenesis in Afroasiatic. In Daniel Barreteau (ed.), Langues et cultures dans le bassin du lac Tchad: journees d'etudes, Paris, ORSTOM, 4-5 septembre 1984 (Colloques et Seminaires), 193-216. Paris: Editions de l'ORSTOM. ISBN 2-7099-0890-5. (author printed as 'Ekkehard WOLFF (University of Hamburg)'; Glottolog ref 108198; IRD Horizon fdi:25270)
sources.note: Podoko is a named case in two places. pp. 201-202: tone in Podoko is argued (after Wolff 1985c, forthcoming) to have developed language-internally from a Proto-Podoko tonal-accent system with grammatically conditioned prosodic marking of nouns; worked example tone class 3 kada 'dog', whose present H-H plus floating L ('H-H-L' on a disyllable) is derived from a modified trisyllabic stem */kada-CV/ with a depressor-initial low-pitched suffix that forced penultimate tonal accent (+H); the suffix segments were lost, leaving the accentual H and a floating low (= downstep). sec. 2.9, pp. 208-209: P…

sources.note: Per the author's own summary in Wolff 1987: 201-202 ('I have argued there that Proto-Podoko had a system with grammatically conditioned prosodic specification at least for nouns'): derives the present Podoko tone system (H vs L with downstep, noun tone classes) from a Proto-Podoko tonal-accent system - modified noun stems with a depressor-initial, low-pitched suffix took obligatory penultimate tonal accent (+H); loss of the suffix left H plus a floating low, explaining downstep and the three-tone melodies on disyllabic nouns (e.g. kada 'dog'); content of the paper itself unseen.
